newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagrebacka sees 1996 group retained at HRK186 mln. [corrected 17:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Zagrebacka sees 1996 group retained at HRK186 mln. [corrected 17:00 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects headline and first paragraph to make clear that forecast is for retained, not net profit.)
Zagrebacka Banka, one of two Croatian companies listed in London, sees the group 1996 retained profit at 186 million kuna compared to nil in 1995, a top bank official said on Tuesday.
"Retained profit for the group is calculated at 185.9 million. The bank should have 156 million kuna after tax and dividend payments," board member Davor Holjevac told Reuters by telephone.
The parent Zagrebacka Banka will propose a dividend of six percent on the 100 German marks face value per ordinary share to the annual meeting on June 10, Holjevac said.
It paid shareholders an equivalent in kuna of five marks a share on the 1995 results.

Earlier today, Zagrebacka group announced a pre-tax profit of 349 million kuna for last year. It gave no figures for the 1996 net. Parent earnings rose to 266 million kuna from the 1995's 162 million before taxation. (Corrects to make clear that it gave no figures for 1996 net profit.)
The group made a 184 million kuna net (corrects by inserting dropped word "net") loss in 1995 after heavy writeoffs on holdings in Croatia's tourist trade.
It comprises Zagrebacka Banka, another bank Pomorska Banka, insurer Adriatic Osiguranje and a holding company that takes care of investments in hoteliers.

The group balance sheet was said to have grown some 18 percent last year from roughly 17.1 billion kuna at the end of 1995, with the bank's assets growth was slightly lower at 16 percent from 16.2 billion in 1995.
